qa.a: Q is equally far from A and B, so PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB
qa.e: Points equidistant from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB, which passes through the midpoint P.

qa.q: To draw a perpendicular from a point Q outside a line, what is the first step?
qa.a: With centre Q, draw an arc cutting the line at two points
qa.e: The two cutting points are equally far from Q; then we find another point equally far from them.

qa.q: A rope is knotted into 12 equal parts to make a right angle. How are the parts shared among the three sides?
qa.e: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12, and a 3-4-5 triangle has a right angle.

qa.q: In a 3-4-5 rope triangle, each part is 50 cm. How long is the longest side?
qa.e: 5 parts × 50 cm = 250 cm.

qa.q: What were the Sulba-Sutras used for?
qa.a: Building fire altars of exact shapes and sizes
qa.e: They gave geometric rules, including right angles made with ropes, for building altars.

qa.q: Which other knotted-rope triangle also gives a right angle?
How many equal parts are needed in total for a 5-12-13 rope triangle?
Which tools are needed to copy an angle exactly?
qa.a: A ruler and a compass only
qa.e: Arcs of equal radius and one copied distance are enough.

qa.q: What is the first step in copying ∠ABC?
qa.a: With centre B, draw an arc cutting both arms
qa.e: The arc from the vertex marks equal distances on both arms.

qa.q: After the first arc, what is drawn at the new point Q?
qa.a: An arc with centre Q and the same radius
qa.e: Using the same radius makes QR equal to BD.

qa.q: Which distance is copied with the compass in the third step?
qa.a: The distance DE between the points where the first arc cut the arms
qa.e: Copying DE gives the third pair of equal sides.

qa.q: Why is the copied angle equal to the original?
qa.a: The two triangles are congruent by SSS
qa.e: BD = QR, BE = QS and DE = RS, so the triangles are congruent and the matching angles are equal.

qa.q: To draw a line through P parallel to l, which angle do we copy?
qa.a: The angle a transversal makes with l, placed at P in the corresponding position
qa.e: Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel.

qa.q: A transversal makes 72° with l. What angle must be copied at P, in the corresponding position, for a parallel line?
qa.e: Corresponding angles must be equal: 72°.

qa.q: Suppose you copy the 72° angle at P in the alternate position instead. Is the new line still parallel to l?
qa.a: Yes — equal alternate angles also give parallel lines
qa.e: Equal alternate angles also show that two lines are parallel.

qa.q: Four angles meet at a point: 150°, 90°, 70° and x. What is x?
qa.e: Angles around a point add to 360°: 360° − 150° − 90° − 70° = 50°.

qa.q: A regular hexagon is made of 6 equilateral triangles. What is each angle of the hexagon?
qa.e: At each corner of the hexagon, two triangle angles meet: 60° + 60° = 120°.

qa.q: With the compass open to the circle's radius, how many steps fit around the circle?
qa.e: Each step makes an equilateral triangle with the centre, so 360° ÷ 60° = 6 steps.

qa.q: What is the perimeter of a regular hexagon with side 5 cm?
qa.e: 6 equal sides: 6 × 5 = 30 cm.

qa.q: A pointed arch has a span of 6 m. What radius should each arc have?
qa.e: In a pointed arch, each arc's radius equals the span.

qa.q: In a pointed arch with span AB, the arc with centre A and the arc with centre B (both of radius AB) meet at the top point C. What kind of triangle is ABC?
qa.e: AC is a radius of the arc centred at A, and BC is a radius of the arc centred at B. Both radii equal the span AB, so all three sides are equal.

qa.q: In an eye design, two equal arcs pass through A and B. Where are the centres of the two arcs?
qa.a: On the perpendicular bisector of AB
qa.e: Each centre is equally far from A and B, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector.

qa.q: A 6-pointed star is drawn from two overlapping equilateral triangles. How many points does it have?
qa.e: Each triangle gives 3 points, and they don't overlap: 3 + 3 = 6.

qa.q: How can you construct a 30° angle with a ruler and a compass?
qa.e: 60° ÷ 2 = 30°, so bisecting a constructed 60° angle gives 30°.

qa.q: What angle do you get by bisecting a right angle?
qa.e: A right angle is 90°. Half of it is 45°.

qa.q: Riya constructs a 60° angle, then another 60° angle right next to it from the same vertex. What angle do the outer arms make?
To construct a square ABCD with side 4 cm, Arjun draws AB = 4 cm. What should he do next?
qa.a: Make a 90° angle at A and mark AD = 4 cm
qa.e: A square has right angles and equal sides, so the next side starts at 90° from AB and is also 4 cm.

qa.q: Kabir draws a circle with his compass opened to 3 cm. What is the diameter of the circle?
qa.e: The compass opening is the radius (3 cm). Diameter = 2 × radius = 6 cm.

qa.q: Which two constructed angles, placed side by side, make 135°?
qa.e: 90° + 45° = 135°. Both can be made with a compass.

qa.q: Aisha constructs a rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
qa.e: Perimeter = 2 × (5 + 3) = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

qa.q: In the 60° construction, why is the angle exactly 60°?
qa.a: The vertex and the two arc points form an equilateral triangle, whose angles are all 60°
qa.e: All three distances are the same compass radius, so the triangle is equilateral and each angle is 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

qa.q: In a floor of square tiles, how many squares meet at each corner point?
qa.e: Each square corner is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4 squares.

qa.q: How many equilateral triangles meet at a point in a triangle tiling?
qa.e: Each angle is 60°. 360° ÷ 60° = 6 triangles.

qa.q: Each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°. How many hexagons meet at a point in a honeycomb tiling?
qa.e: 360° ÷ 120° = 3 hexagons.

qa.q: Why can't regular pentagons tile a floor on their own?
qa.a: Their 108° angles do not fit into 360° a whole number of times
qa.e: 3 pentagons make 324° (gap) and 4 make 432° (overlap). No whole number gives exactly 360°.

qa.q: Regular octagons (135° each) and squares tile together. At each point, 2 octagons meet. How many squares are needed there?
qa.e: 2 × 135° = 270°. 360° − 270° = 90°, which is exactly one square corner.

qa.q: At a point in a tiling, the angles are 90°, 60°, 60° and x. What is x?
qa.e: All angles around the point add up to 360°. x = 360° − 90° − 60° − 60° = 150°.

qa.q: Which shape can NOT tile a floor on its own?
qa.e: A regular octagon has 135° angles. 2 × 135° = 270° and 3 × 135° = 405°, so octagons alone leave gaps.

qa.q: Meena's room floor is 3 m by 2 m. She uses square tiles of side 50 cm. How many tiles does she need?
qa.e: Along 3 m: 300 ÷ 50 = 6 tiles. Along 2 m: 200 ÷ 50 = 4 tiles. Total = 6 × 4 = 24 tiles.

qa.q: How many pieces does a tangram have?
qa.e: 2 large, 1 medium and 2 small triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram: 7 pieces.

qa.q: How many of the tangram pieces are triangles?
qa.e: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small = 5 triangles.

qa.q: The whole tangram square has area 16 units. What is the area of one large triangle?
qa.e: Each large triangle is a quarter of the whole square: 16 ÷ 4 = 4.

qa.q: The whole tangram square has area 16 units. What is the area of the small square piece?
qa.e: The square piece is made of two small triangles (1 unit each): 2 units.

qa.q: Can a 5 × 5 grid be tiled exactly by 2 × 1 dominoes?
qa.a: No — 25 squares is odd, but each domino covers 2
qa.e: 12 dominoes cover 24 squares, leaving 1 square; 13 would need 26 squares.

qa.q: How many 2 × 1 dominoes are needed to tile a 4 × 6 grid?
qa.e: 4 × 6 = 24 squares, and each domino covers 2: 24 ÷ 2 = 12.

qa.q: Two opposite corners are removed from an 8 × 8 chessboard. How many squares are left?
qa.e: 64 − 2 = 62 squares.

qa.q: Why can't 31 dominoes cover the chessboard with two opposite corners removed?
qa.a: Both removed squares are the same colour, leaving 32 of one colour and 30 of the other
qa.e: Each domino covers one black and one white square, so we would need equal numbers of each colour.

qa.q: Which artist is famous for tilings made of interlocking birds, fish and lizards?
qa.e: M. C. Escher, a Dutch artist, created many such tilings.

qa.q: What shape are the cells in a honeycomb?
qa.e: Bees build six-sided (hexagonal) cells.

qa.q: Why are hexagons a good shape for bees?
qa.a: They fit with no gaps and use less wax for the space they hold
qa.e: Hexagons tile without gaps and need less wall material than squares or triangles holding the same space.

qa.q: What was special about the 'hat' tile discovered in 2023?
qa.a: It tiles a floor but never in a repeating pattern
qa.e: It is the first known single shape that can only tile without ever repeating.

qa.q: How many sides does the 'hat' tile have?
qa.e: The hat is a 13-sided shape.

qa.q: How can you make an Escher-style tile from a square?
qa.a: Cut a piece from one side and stick it on the opposite side
qa.e: The bump on one side matches the dent on the next tile, so there are still no gaps.

qa.q: In the middle of a honeycomb, how many neighbouring cells does each hexagonal cell touch?
qa.e: Each of its 6 sides is shared with one neighbouring cell.

qa.q: What shape are the cells of a paper wasp's nest?
qa.e: Wasps also build hexagonal cells that fit together without gaps.

qa.q: Left pan: 3 bags of x kg and 2 kg. Right pan: 11 kg. Which equation shows this?
qa.e: Three bags weigh 3x, plus 2 kg, balancing 11 kg.

qa.q: Solve 3x + 2 = 11 for the bag weight x.
qa.e: Remove 2 from both sides: 3x = 9. Then x = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

qa.q: In that balance (3 bags + 2 kg on the left, 11 kg on the right), 2 kg is removed from both pans. What is left?
qa.e: Removing the same weight from both sides keeps the balance: 3x = 9.

qa.q: Which action keeps a balanced scale balanced?
qa.e: Whatever we do to one side we must do to the other.

qa.q: Matchstick triangles in a row use 2n + 1 sticks. Which step uses 61 sticks?
By trying values one by one, find x in 7x − 4 = 59.
qa.e: x = 8 gives 52, x = 9 gives 63 − 4 = 59 ✓.

qa.q: Why is trial and error often slow?
qa.a: We may need many guesses, especially when the answer is large or a fraction
qa.e: Guessing works, but a systematic method reaches the answer in a few steps.

qa.q: Left pan: 5 bags. Right pan: 2 bags and 12 kg. How heavy is each bag?
qa.e: Remove 2 bags from both pans: 3 bags = 12 kg, so each bag = 4 kg.

qa.q: Which of these is an equation?
qa.e: Only 4x − 1 = 11 has an = sign joining two sides.

qa.q: Is x = 3 the solution of 2x + 5 = 11?
qa.e: Put x = 3: 2 × 3 + 5 = 6 + 5 = 11. Both sides are 11, so x = 3 is the solution.

qa.q: Arjun is a years old. In 5 years he will be 17. Which equation fits?
qa.e: In 5 years his age will be a + 5, and that equals 17.

qa.q: Solve x + 9 = 20.
qa.e: Which number plus 9 makes 20? 20 − 9 = 11. Check: 11 + 9 = 20.

qa.q: 6 pens cost ₹90. If one pen costs p rupees, then 6p = 90. What is p?
Which value of y makes 3y − 4 = 14 true?
Meena cut a ribbon of length L cm into 4 equal pieces of 15 cm each. So L ÷ 4 = 15. What is L?
Kabir thinks of a number n, multiplies it by 3, then subtracts 5 and gets 16. Which equation shows this?
qa.e: First multiply by 3 (3n), then subtract 5 (3n − 5). The result is 16.

qa.q: Solve x − 7 = 12.
qa.e: Add 7 to both sides: x = 12 + 7 = 19. Check: 19 − 7 = 12.

qa.q: Solve 5y = 35.
qa.e: Divide both sides by 5: y = 35 ÷ 5 = 7.

qa.q: Solve 3x + 4 = 19.
qa.e: Subtract 4: 3x = 15. Divide by 3: x = 5. Check: 3 × 5 + 4 = 19.

qa.q: What is the best first step to solve 4x − 3 = 21?
qa.e: Undo the − 3 first by adding 3 to both sides: 4x = 24. Then divide by 4.

qa.q: Solve a ÷ 4 + 2 = 6.
qa.e: Subtract 2: a ÷ 4 = 4. Multiply by 4: a = 16. Check: 16 ÷ 4 + 2 = 6.

qa.q: Solve 2(x + 3) = 18.
qa.e: Divide both sides by 2: x + 3 = 9. Subtract 3: x = 6. Check: 2 × (6 + 3) = 18.

qa.q: Solve 7 = 2y − 5.
qa.e: Add 5 to both sides: 12 = 2y. Divide by 2: y = 6. Check: 2 × 6 − 5 = 7.

qa.q: Riya says the solution of 3x + 6 = 21 is x = 9. What is the correct solution?
qa.e: Check x = 9: 3 × 9 + 6 = 33, not 21. Correct: 3x = 21 − 6 = 15, so x = 5.

qa.q: Solve x + 9 = 4.
qa.e: Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 4 − 9 = −5.

qa.q: Solve −3x = 12.
qa.e: Divide both sides by −3: x = 12 ÷ (−3) = −4.

qa.q: Solve 2x = 7.
Solve (2/5)x = 6.
qa.e: Divide by 2/5, which means multiply by 5/2: 6 × 5/2 = 15.

qa.q: Solve 6y + 7 = 4y + 21.
Solve 5x − 3 = 2x + 9.
In 3x + 8 = 20, the +8 is moved to the right side. What does the equation become?
qa.e: A term that moves across the = sign changes sign: +8 becomes −8.

qa.q: In 4x = 28, the 4 is moved to the right side. What does the equation become?
qa.e: A multiplier on one side becomes a divisor on the other.

qa.q: Which equation has the solution x = 5?
qa.e: 2 × 5 + 3 = 13 ✓. The others are solved by x = 4, x = 0 and x = 6.

qa.q: Start with x = 3, multiply by 4 and then subtract 2. Which equation do you get?
Which equation has no solution?
qa.e: Taking x from both sides leaves 4 = 7, which is never true.

qa.q: If 4k + 1 = 13, what is 8k + 2?
If 3m − 2 = 10, what is 6m − 4?
If 3m − 2 = 10, what is m + 1?
qa.e: 3m = 12, so m = 4 and m + 1 = 5.

qa.q: A machine multiplies by 3 and then subtracts 4. The output is 23. What was the input?
qa.e: Undo in reverse: 23 + 4 = 27, then 27 ÷ 3 = 9.

qa.q: A machine adds 5 and then multiplies by 2. The output is 30. What was the input?
qa.e: Undo in reverse: 30 ÷ 2 = 15, then 15 − 5 = 10.

qa.q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is 41. What is the smaller number?
qa.e: n + (n + 1) = 41, so 2n + 1 = 41, 2n = 40 and n = 20. The numbers are 20 and 21.

qa.q: A father is 3 times as old as his son Kabir. Their ages add up to 48 years. How old is Kabir?
qa.e: Let Kabir be x. Father = 3x. x + 3x = 4x = 48, so x = 12. Father is 36. Check: 12 + 36 = 48.

qa.q: A rectangle's length is 3 cm more than its breadth. Its perimeter is 26 cm. What is the breadth?
qa.e: Breadth b, length b + 3. Perimeter 2(b + b + 3) = 26, so 2b + 3 = 13, 2b = 10, b = 5 cm. Length is 8 cm. Check: 2 × (5 + 8) = 26.

qa.q: A triangle has angles x, x and 80°. What is x?
Aisha has ₹50 more than Harpreet. Together they have ₹230. How much does Harpreet have?
qa.e: Harpreet h, Aisha h + 50. h + h + 50 = 230, so 2h = 180 and h = ₹90. Aisha has ₹140. Check: 90 + 140 = 230.

qa.q: Train tickets cost ₹35 each. A group pays ₹420 in all. How many tickets did they buy?
I think of a number, multiply it by 4, add 10 and get 50. What is my number?
Joseph buys 3 notebooks and a pen that costs ₹5. He pays ₹95 in all. What does one notebook cost?
Rohan wrote 2x + 5 = 13 → 2x = 18 → x = 9. What went wrong?
qa.a: He added 5 instead of subtracting it; it should be 2x = 8
qa.e: To undo + 5 we subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 8.

qa.q: What is the correct solution of 2x + 5 = 13?
Meena wrote 3x + 4 = 19 → 7x = 19. What is the mistake?
qa.a: She joined 3x and 4, which are unlike terms
qa.e: A number cannot be added to an x-term. Subtract 4 instead: 3x = 15.

qa.q: What is the correct solution of 3x + 4 = 19?
Arjun wrote 5x = 20 → x = 100. What is the mistake?
qa.a: He multiplied by 5 instead of dividing by 5
qa.e: 5x means 5 × x, so we undo it by dividing: x = 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

qa.q: Kiran wrote 3(x + 2) = 21 → 3x + 2 = 21. What is the correct value of x?
qa.e: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6 = 21, so 3x = 15 and x = 5. (Or divide first: x + 2 = 7.)

qa.q: Riya wrote x − 6 = 10 → x = 4. What is the correct value of x?
qa.e: Undo − 6 by adding 6: x = 10 + 6 = 16.

qa.q: What is the best way to catch a mistake in a solution?
qa.a: Put the answer back into the original equation
qa.e: If both sides are equal after substituting, the answer is right.

qa.q: What is Bījagaṇita?
qa.e: Bījagaṇita means algebra; Bhāskara II wrote a book with this title.

qa.q: In old Indian algebra, what did 'yā' stand for?
qa.e: 'yā' was used like our x; 'rū' marked known numbers.

qa.q: In old Indian notation, what did a dot over a number mean?
qa.e: A dot over a number showed that it was negative (like a debt).

qa.q: Use x = (D − B) ÷ (A − C) to solve 7x + 3 = 4x + 18.
Use Brahmagupta's rule to solve 9x + 2 = 5x + 30.
From the Bakhshali manuscript: B gets 2 times A, C gets 3 times B and D gets 4 times C. Together they get 132. How much does A get?
In the same problem (A gets 4), how much does D get?
Puzzle: a merchant sells 5 of his horses to pay a debt and is left with 2/3 of them. How many horses did he have?
qa.e: Selling 5 removed 1/3 of the horses, so 1/3 of the total is 5 and the total is 15. (x − 5 = 2x/3 gives x = 15.)

qa.q: Think of n. Double it and add 10, then halve the result. Which expression do you have now?
In the same trick, you now subtract the number you first thought of. What is the result if you started with 7?
qa.e: (2 × 7 + 10) ÷ 2 − 7 = 12 − 7 = 5. It is 5 for every starting number.

qa.q: Trick: think of a number, multiply by 4, add 20, divide by 4, subtract the number. What is the result?
Which trick always ends with 3?
qa.e: (2n + 6) ÷ 2 − n = n + 3 − n = 3. The others give 1.5, n + 6 and 1.

qa.q: Children and donkeys have 20 heads and 56 feet in all. How many donkeys are there?
With 20 heads and 56 feet (8 donkeys), how many children are there?
There are 30 heads and 84 feet (children and donkeys). With d donkeys, which equation fits?
qa.e: Children = 30 − d with 2 feet each; donkeys = d with 4 feet each.

qa.q: Solve 2(30 − d) + 4d = 84 to find the number of donkeys.
